- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp sentiment spikes (≥0.67 with +0.67+ sentiment change), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% for next 2–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume remains high, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- When sentiment change is negative and recent price is rising, model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–7 day horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (±0.33+ change over 3–5 days), model tends to overfit short-term noise; apply smoothing or reduce amplitude by 1–3%.
- If news volume is high and sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often overreacts; dampen forecast by 1–2% for 1–5 day horizons.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often misses the momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently low and price is trending down, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- If sentiment change is positive and recent price is falling, model often fails to capture reversal; increase forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- When sentiment is high and price is falling, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
